## Where he is pointing, and where everyone else is

1. The Reuters panel and the "MOTO 509" plate both read the right way round to us rather

2. Every cyclist is facing us, so the road runs roughly along the taking camera's line

3. His body is square to the bike — the torso below the helmet is a black polo shirt

The relative sizes give the distances. His crash helmet is about twice as wide in the
frame as the race leader's cycling helmet, so the leader is roughly twice as far from the
taking camera as he is: a few metres straight back. Turning the image positions into real
offsets (object size × pixel offset ÷ object width in pixels, which is independent of the

helmet, the riders in blue and white, the orange Euskaltel jersey) are only about
0.7–1.1 m off that side while being metres further back, i.e. no more than about 20°
round from straight behind him.

Because he is aiming across the road while the entire bunch is lined up behind him, every
cyclist in this picture lies about **60°–85° outside his camera's line of sight**. That

So the honest answer is: **at his current angle, not one of the cyclists visible in this

## What his photograph would actually contain

His frame would be filled by what is beside and slightly ahead of him on that side: the

The conclusion depends on his head being turned roughly square to the road rather than
